codeReview.summary: The round-two fix resolves the prior blocker: it adds a test seam for Win32Window monitor refresh rate, drives a 60 Hz to 144 Hz change through WinSwiftUIWindowHost.windowDidChangeDisplay(_:) and now asserts both timer cadence and runtime minimum-frame-interval updates for VAL-CROSS-009.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Windows worker bootstrap still has a tooling gap: the init entrypoint is a bash-only wrapper even though this mission runs on Windows, so the worker had to bypass the documented init step and call windows-swift-env.ps1 directly.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/init.sh:1-5 is a bash script that only forwards to windows-swift-env.ps1 -CheckOnly; the fix handoff skillFeedback and transcript skeleton show bash .factory/init.sh failed in this Windows environment and the worker switched to the PowerShell command directly.

summary: Pass: the new fix closes the remaining VAL-CROSS-009 gap by exercising a real monitorRefreshRate change through WinSwiftUIWindowHost and asserting the resulting timer and runtime pacing updates.
